newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices bounce back after setback.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices bounce back after setback.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Tuesday bounced back on the local market after modest setback on Monday, dealers said.
Fresh consumer buying dragged prices upward after recent losses while limited arrivals kept offerings at a low ebb.

In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 10 rupees at 1,410/1,445 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved up by 25 rupees at 1,465/1,500 rupees per quintal. Sugar was down by 8/20 rupees per quintal on Monday.
"Thin supplies from mills to the market helped prices to bounce back," one broker said.
"Local millers are witnessing a higher offtake by neighbouring states which in turn had curtailed supplies of sugar from mills to the Bombay market," he said.
Sugar mill delivery moved up to 1,360/1,375 rupees from 1,325/1,345 rupees per quintal on higher outstation buying at the mill level.

Dealers said the market bounced back on a shortage of ready stock despite a higher release of free sale quota as some traders feared that a major part of the free sale quota for this month have gone unofficially from India to the neighbouring countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh as sugar prices in these countries are booming compared to Indian market.
Free sale quota for current month is 800,000 tonnes (including 50,000 additional quota) against 700,000 tonnes released last month.
